title: Compact pushout presentations survive arrow retracts
statement: Fix a universe $\mathcal U$; small means $\mathcal U$-small. Let $\tau\in\mathcal U$ be an uncountable regular cardinal, where regular means that a union of fewer than $\tau$ sets each of cardinality less than $\tau$ has cardinality less than $\tau$. A category is $\tau$-filtered if every diagram with fewer than $\tau$ morphisms has a cocone. An object is $\tau$-presentable if its Hom functor preserves small $\tau$-filtered colimits. Let $\mathcal A$ be an ordinary category with small Hom sets and all small colimits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], generated under small $\tau$-filtered colimits by a small family of $\tau$-presentable objects. A pushout means a colimit of a span. Let $u:P\to Q$ be a morphism between $\tau$-presentable objects. Let $g:V\to W$ be its pushout along some $P\to V$. Suppose $g':V'\to W'$ is a retract of $g$ in the arrow category: there are commuting squares $s:g'\to g$ and $r:g\to g'$ with $rs=1_{g'}$ (the arrow category has arrows as objects and commuting squares as morphisms). There exist $\tau$-presentable objects $P',Q'$, a map $u':P'\to Q'$ and a map $P'\to V'$ such that $g'$ is a pushout of $u'$ along that map and $u'$ belongs to the weakly saturated closure of $\{u\}$. Here the weakly saturated closure is the smallest arrow class containing $u$ and all isomorphisms and closed under pushouts, small continuous transfinite compositions and arrow retracts; continuous means that each nonzero limit stage is the colimit of its predecessors. No presentability of $V,V',W,W'$ is assumed.
